title: Magnitude Versus Intensity Map
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: One magnitude pinned to a banner while a field of Modified Mercalli intensities appears beneath it, computed from the Allen, Wald and Worden (2012) intensity prediction equation with per-town site amplification.

learningObjectives: Differentiate magnitude, which describes the earthquake, from intensity, which describes a place.
Analyse how depth, distance and local ground conditions change the intensity at a given place.
Explain why a town further from the epicentre can shake harder than a nearer one.
Convert a magnitude difference into an energy ratio.
prerequisites: Chapter 11: the Mercalli intensity scale and the moment magnitude scale

keyQuestions: How many magnitudes does one earthquake have, and how many intensities?
Why did Mexico City suffer so badly 350 km from the 1985 epicentre?
What does the same magnitude do differently at 10 km depth and at 250 km?
How much more energy is a magnitude 7 than a magnitude 5?
commonMisconceptions: Magnitude and intensity are two names for the same thing.
The nearest place to the epicentre always shakes hardest.
A high magnitude always means severe damage.
Intensity VIII is twice as strong as intensity IV.
assessmentOpportunities: Reads six different intensities off one magnitude and explains the spread.
Predicts the effect of switching a town from bedrock to artificial fill.
Assigns a Mercalli grade from an effect description in the Did You Feel It mode.
